scope: Primary sources for resorption and parasitic plant routes; host production, allometry and release conditions are committed project products named in growth.py INPUT_FILES.

sources.citation: Vergutz, L., Manzoni, S., Porporato, A., Novais, R. F. and Jackson, R. B. (2012). Global resorption efficiencies and concentrations of carbon and nutrients in leaves of terrestrial plants. Ecological Monographs 82(2), 205-220.
sources.use: Mean phosphorus resorption 64.9% (nitrogen 62.1%) across about 1,000 data points from 86 studies; resorption falls as nutrient status rises.
sources.limit: Terrestrial leaves; used as the central resorption for an aerophyte's active tissue.

sources.citation: Glatzel, G. and Geils, B. W. (2009). Mistletoe ecophysiology: host-parasite interactions. Botany 87(1), 10-15.
sources.use: Xylem-tapping hemiparasites draw water and inorganic nutrients from host xylem through the haustorium and photosynthesise; leaf P of Loranthus europaeus tracks its host Quercus petraea (Fig. 2).
sources.limit: No N or P flux figures. The abstract's phloem statements refer to holoparasitic forms; the body text is cited for the xylem route.

sources.citation: Birschwilks, M., Haupt, S., Hofius, D. and Neumann, S. (2006). Journal of Experimental Botany 57(4), 911-921 (title not recorded here).
sources.use: Host phloem is continuous with Cuscuta phloem; transfer of sucrose and amino acids is non-selective.
